'''Pondicherry Airport''' {{Airport codes|PNY|VOPC}} is a [[domestic airport]] serving the [[union territory]] of [[Puducherry (union territory)|Puducherry]], [[India]]. It is located at [[Lawspet]], situated {{cvt|8.1|km}} from the international community of [[Auroville]]. The airport has scheduled flights and operations of the local flying training school. In 2007, the [[Government of Puducherry]] decided to expand the airport to accommodate larger aircraft and commissioned a new terminal building.<ref name= IBN>{{cite news|title=Flight operations await new terminal |url=http://ibnlive.in.com/news/flight-operations-await-new-terminal/256422-60-118.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120513121042/http://ibnlive.in.com/news/flight-operations-await-new-terminal/256422-60-118.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=13 May 2012|publisher=[[IBN Live]] |date= 10 May 2012 |access-date=3 July 2012}}</ref> The new terminal was inaugurated on 18 January 2013, with the arrival of a [[SpiceJet]] flight from [[Kempegowda International Airport|Bangalore]].<ref>{{cite news|title=First flight to Pondicherry from Bangalore on January 17 |website=[[The Hindu]] |date=5 January 2013 |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/first-flight-to-puducherry-from-bangalore-on-january-17/article4277106.ece |access-date=6 January 2013}}</ref> After a gap of three years, the airport was operationalised again under the [[UDAN]] scheme in August 2017, with daily flights to [[Rajiv Gandhi International Airport|Hyderabad]] and Bangalore.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/puducherry/spicejet-to-operate-daily-flights-between-hyderabad-and-puducherry-starting-august-16/articleshow/59632657.cms|title=SpiceJet to operate daily flights between Hyderabad and Puducherry starting August 16|work=The Times of India|access-date=2017-10-31}}</ref>

On 18 August 2024, [[Minister of Defence (India)|Defence Minister]] [[Rajnath Singh]] inaugurated a [[Indian Coast Guard#Organisation|Coast Guard Air Enclave]] (CGAE) at the airport. A [[HAL Dhruv]] and [[Aérospatiale Alouette III|HAL Chetak]] squadron will be based at the CGAE.<ref>{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2024-08-18 |title=Rajnath Singh inaugurates new maritime rescue coordination centre in Chennai |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/rajnath-singh-inaugurates-new-maritime-rescue-coordination-centre-in-chennai/article68540170.ece |access-date=2024-08-19 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

== History ==
The airport was constructed in 1989. Between that year and 1991, regional airline [[Vayudoot]] flew to [[Madras]], [[Neyveli]], and [[Bangalore]], however the flights were not successful and all were ended. The airport remained in disuse for the following two decades.<ref name=pondy3jan>[https://web.archive.org/web/20140116064542/http://www.newindianexpress.com/states/tamil_nadu/article1405082.ece SpiceJet announces Pondy flight schedule]. The New Indian Express. 3 January 2013. Retrieved 7 December 2015.</ref>

In June 2007, a [[memorandum of understanding]] (MoU) was signed between the local government and the [[Airports Authority of India]] (AAI) for expansion of the airport. For the first phase, 19.92 hectares of land were acquired at {{Indian Rupee}} 18.95 crore. Then the new terminal was constructed and the runway extended by 260 m (853 ft), allowing for the landing of [[ATR (aircraft manufacturer)|ATR]] aircraft. This phase was completed in late 2012. The second phase of expansion involves acquiring 200 more acres of land to extend the runway by an additional 1,100 m (3,609 ft), allowing larger [[jet aircraft]] to land at the airport.<ref>{{cite news|title=Pondicherry airport to go on stream in October|url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2011-09-03/news/30110146_1_pondicherry-airport-runway-lawspet|work=[[The Economic Times]] |date= 3 September 2011 |access-date=3 January 2012}}{{dead link|date=October 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>
The new terminal was inaugurated with the arrival of a [[SpiceJet]] Bombardier Dash 8 Q400 aircraft on 17 January 2013 from [[Bangalore]]. However, this daily service lasted for only a little over one year as the airline withdrew the flight citing low number of passengers.<ref name=pondy3jan /><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/with-last-flight-puducherry-airport-runs-out-of-steam/article5640023.ece|title=With last flight, Pondicherry airport runs out of steam|author=Jaisankar, C.|date=31 January 2014|work=[[The Hindu]]|access-date=7 December 2015}}</ref> The following year, the airport once again was brought back into operation when [[Air India Regional|Alliance Air]] commenced flights from Bangalore on 14 April 2015, subsidised by the Pondicherry Government. These flights were suspended six months later due to "payment issues".<ref name=alliancesuspension>{{cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/puducherry/puducherrys-flight-services-suspended-temporarily/article7778903.ece |title= Puducherry's flight services suspended temporarily|newspaper= The Hindu|date= 19 October 2015|last1= Philip|first1= Annie}}</ref>

In October 2016, the Pondicherry government signed a Tripartite MoU with the Ministry of Civil Aviation (MoCA) and AAI in New Delhi to operationalise the airport under the Regional Connectivity Scheme.<ref>{{cite news|title=Puducherry Airport To Be Operational From January 2017|url=https://www.ndtv.com/south/puducherry-airport-to-be-operational-from-january-2017-1468727|publisher=[[NDTV]] |date=1 October 2016|access-date=4 September 2018}}</ref> Subsequently, SpiceJet was awarded the Hyderabad-Pondicherry route under the scheme in March 2017<ref>{{cite news|title=SpiceJet awarded six routes under regional connectivity scheme|url=https://ultra.news/t-t/30139/spicejet-awarded-six-routes-regional-connectivity-scheme|publisher=Ultra News|date=30 March 2017|access-date=4 September 2018|archive-date=4 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180904192246/https://ultra.news/t-t/30139/spicejet-awarded-six-routes-regional-connectivity-scheme|url-status=dead}}</ref> and the airline commenced operations from 16 August 2017.<ref>{{cite news|title=Puducherry back on aviation map; services to Hyderabad launched|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/india/puducherry-back-on-aviation-map-services-to-hyderabad-launched-4799226/|work=[[The Indian Express]] |date=16 August 2017|access-date=4 September 2018}}</ref> SpiceJet later resumed its flight to Bangalore from Pondicherry in February 2018.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bangalore-UT flight service resumes|url=https://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-tamilnadu/flight-service-to-bangalore-resumes/article22767470.ece|work=[[The Hindu]] |date=16 February 2018|access-date=4 September 2018}}{{dead link|date=September 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

==Structure==

Puducherry Airport has one asphalt runway, oriented 07/25, 1500 m long and 30 m wide. It has a 100 m by 150 m [[Airport ramp|apron]] and its new terminal building can handle 300 passengers during peak hours. Navigational aids at Puducherry include an [[aerodrome beacon]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Airport website |url=http://www.aai.aero/allAirports/pondicherry_technicalinfo.jsp |access-date=3 January 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120102155608/http://www.aai.aero/allAirports/pondicherry_technicalinfo.jsp |archive-date=2 January 2012 }}</ref> Currently land is being acquired to extend the runway and accommodate larger aircraft to increase flight services and open the airport for international flights.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/india/efforts-on-to-expand-puducherry-airport-runway-cm-narayanasamy/|title=Efforts on to expand Puducherry airport runway: CM Narayanasamy|date=2017-08-03|work=The Indian Express|access-date=2017-10-31|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Demands==
There are also demands to operate direct flight services between Puducherry to [[Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport|Mumbai]], [[Indira Gandhi International Airport|Delhi]] and [[Manohar International Airport|Goa]].
